title: A Hollow for the Ember
premise: Rafael Voss has spent nine years copying ledgers for the Emberhold temple, hiding the ember-gift that lets her read the memories of anything she touches. When the crown's witch-hunters arrive and her brother is seized as a 'gifted' criminal, Rafael learns he was taken because their dead mother sold his soul to the court beneath Thornfell to pay a debt of her own. To free him, Rafael must descend into the Undercourt with a disgraced huntress, Sera Ilvane, who has begun to doubt the law she serves—and the two women fall in love even as duty pulls them apart. In the end, Rafael trades her own soul's ember for her brother's, but Sera breaks her oath to forge a false ledger in the court's own records, leaving Rafael alive, unbound, and finally visible.
about_author: Gideon Amberdale is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated letters in a mountain province before turning to fiction. They write about people whose names were never meant to survive the paperwork.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. She copies tithes in the Emberhold scriptorium, concealing the ember-gift that flares when she touches old wax seals. A smuggler's coin she handles shows her a memory of the crown's new edict: all gifted persons to be registered or hunted. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: Snow Before the Bell
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. First snow falls on Thornfell as witch-hunters enter the valley under a white banner. Rafael warns her brother Tomas, a carter on the smuggler roads, to vanish until spring. He refuses—his debts are paid, he says, and he owes no one flight. Beat: stubborn love, first fracture.

chapters.title: What the Wax Remembers
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Touching a temple seal, Rafael glimpses her mother's signature on an old contract: one soul sold to the Undercourt, name smudged. She realizes the debt was never settled—it transferred. Beat: inheritance revealed as a trap, not a gift.

chapters.title: The White Banner Comes
chapters.summary: Sera Ilvane's POV. The huntress leads the seizure of Tomas Voss, reading him his rights by rote while noting he carries no ember at all. Her captain insists the paperwork is sufficient. Beat: Sera's first crack of doubt; justice and procedure diverge.

chapters.title: Ash on the Register
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael petitions the temple to intercede and is refused—the Emberhold protects its ledgers, not its scribes. That night she burns her copy-slots out of the register, erasing herself officially. Beat: grief hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: A Huntress Off the Road
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Rafael ambushes the prisoner convoy on a smuggler's cut and finds Sera alone, separated from her unit. Instead of killing each other, they strike a wary bargain: Sera wants proof the court's soul-contracts are forged; Rafael wants her brother. Beat: enemies bound by mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Catechism
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. On the high passes, Rafael teaches Sera the unwritten laws of the mountain roads—shelter debts, silence tolls, the shrines where even hunters are safe. Sera begins to see justice as something practiced, not decreed. Beat: grudging respect kindling warmth.

chapters.title: The Shrine at Coldwater
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sheltering from a storm, Sera confesses she once reported her own mentor, who died in custody. Rafael, touching the shrine stone, reads the mentor's last memory and gives it to her. Beat: intimacy through shared guilt; love's first unspoken admission.

chapters.title: Tollgate of Teeth
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A bandit toll-gang recognizes Rafael's old routes and demands payment in blood for her years of silence. Sera fights beside her without orders. They win through but Sera takes a wound. Beat: loyalty proven in violence; tenderness in its aftermath.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Both POVs braided. They reach the Undercourt's gate, a cavern city of amber light where souls are held as collateral. Entry requires a debt of one's own. Rafael signs herself in. Beat: awe and horror; point of no return.

chapters.title: Interest Accrued
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The Undercourt's auditor reveals the truth: their mother sold not Tomas's soul but her own—and it defaulted to her children jointly. Freeing Tomas means someone else assumes the bond. Beat: the inheritance theme turned knife-sharp.

chapters.title: The Reading Room of Souls
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera searches the contract archives and discovers systematic forgery: the crown has been manufacturing soul-debts to fund the witch-hunts. She copies evidence, betraying her oath page by page. Beat: duty inverted; she now steals for justice.

chapters.title: Tomas, Unlit
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael reaches Tomas in the holding vaults; his soul-ember is dimmed but intact. He begs her not to trade herself, revealing he has known about her gift for years and kept her secret. Beat: sibling love laid bare; sacrifice refused.

chapters.title: What Duty Owes
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera's captain arrives under truce, offering her reinstatement if she surrenders Rafael and buries the forgery evidence. Sera burns the offer in front of him. Beat: the break with the law made irrevocable and clean.

chapters.title: The Bargain of Embers
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael secretly negotiates with the auditor: her ember for Tomas's freedom, signed before Sera can stop her. Her gift—the thing she hid her whole life—becomes the price of visibility. Beat: tragic irony at full weight.

chapters.title: Ledger, Broken
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Discovering the signed transfer, Sera does the unthinkable: she alters the Undercourt's master record using the forgery techniques she learned, swapping the bonded name for the long-dead auditor's predecessor. Beat: desperate, transgressive hope.

chapters.title: Audit of the Deep Court
chapters.summary: Both POVs. The falsified ledger triggers a formal audit; the court turns on itself as debts unravel. Amid the chaos, Rafael touches the great seal and reads the founding truth: the Undercourt itself was built on a stolen soul. Beat: climax ignites; systems devour themselves.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falls
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Escape through collapsing galleries as winter seals the passes above. Rafael's ember gutters—part of the price already paid—and Sera carries her through the dark. Beat: climax's cost made flesh; love stated plainly at last.

chapters.title: Freeholder's Snow
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. They surface into deep snow with Tomas alive and Rafael dimmed but breathing, her bond voided by the audited records. Sera is officially a deserter; unofficially, the mountains shelter their own. Beat: exhale after catastrophe; chosen exile as homecoming.

chapters.title: The Gift Made Visible
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Recovering in a roadhouse, Rafael stops hiding—she reads memories openly for neighbors seeking lost kin and closed accounts, becoming the valley's unofficial arbiter. Beat: themes resolved; justice outside the law embodied in daily practice.

chapters.title: Amberdale's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Crown investigators arrive following the Undercourt scandal; Sera meets them with the copied evidence and her own confession, forcing the forgery into daylight. The hunt collapses; some hunters defect. Beat: public reckoning; the law forced to face what it served.

chapters.title: A Hollow for the Ember
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, coda. Spring thaw. Rafael, Sera, and Tomas keep the waystation at Coldwater shrine, where travelers leave debts and memories in equal measure. Rafael's ember slowly regrows in the hollow left by what she gave. Final beat: inheritance rewritten—not what we're owed, but what we choose to carry.
